newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN OLOS FUTURES VOLATILE AFTER LEBED SACKING.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN OLOS FUTURES VOLATILE AFTER LEBED SACKING.

text.p: Belgian OLO futures danced about violently on Thursday after Russian President Boris Yeltsin said on national television that he had sacked security chief Alexander Lebed.
"There are almost no prices in Bunds, though Belgium seems to be holding up," one dealer said.
By 1420 GMT December OLO futures were six basis points down at 119.11, with a wide bid/ask spread of 119.10/119.19.
"The market might go down in the next couple of days...but it would be the best moment to buy," the dealer added.

In the underlying cash market, though, prices remained barely changed, with the 10-year OLO yield edging up one basis point from 6.11 percent where it stood before the news to stand unchanged from the previous close at 6.12 percent.
"There is no panic at all in the market," another trader said, adding players were now waiting to see how Lebed would respond. They would get more nervous if Lebed contested Yeltsin's decision.
The 10-year yield spread over equivalent German Bunds wavered between an easier seven and an unchanged eight basis points, which some dealers still consider to be too low.
But the steepness of the yield curve coupled with the prospect of a single European currency was seen keeping the spread low.
"Everything from OLO 20 (2004) onwards is cheaper than Germany and there's lots of liquidity in the Belgian market. This spread can last a few months," one dealer added.
Dealers said a mix of U.S. data this afternoon which sent Treasuries higher was largely shrugged off by the Belgian market
